recentItems.title: Is AI coming for our jobs? I put it to the test at CIFTIS 2026
recentItems.description:
For years, AI has been the future – now it's the present. AI is already analyzing data, making decisions, handling repetitive tasks and stepping into real-world services. So what happens when AI stops being something we use, and starts doing the work itself?

At the China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) 2026, CGTN's Wang Tao put AI to the test: what jobs can it take off our hands, and where do humans still have the upper hand? Is the future of work really a race – or a place where humans and machines each play to their strengths?

recentItems.title: The Heat: US global war on terrorism
recentItems.description:
25 years ago, terrorist attacks on the United States changed the course of history. In response, Washington invaded Afghanistan and launched the Global War on Terror. But a quarter-century later, what were the lasting consequences? 

The Heat host: Sean Callebs 
Guests:
Amir Handjani is board member for the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft.
Hafed Al Ghwell is director emeritus and senior advisor at The Stimson Center. 
Peter Kuznick is professor of history at American University.
Edmund Ghareeb is an academic and expert on Middle East Affairs.

recentItems.title: 160,000-year-old Denisovan fossils found in Yunnan: What do they reveal?
recentItems.description:
CGTN Europe spoke to Dr. Hao Li, research professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, following the discovery of 160,000-year-old Denisovan bone and tooth fossils in Yunnan Province. Dr. Li breaks down how the fossils at Bianfu Cave fill a critical gap in the archaeological record of southwestern China, what stone and bone tools reveal about Denisovan adaptability, and evidence showing how these ancient hominins hunted and survived.
